_comment: The libgit2 port campaign's decomposition, as specs/planning/decomposition.md describes, of the two link units the build links (crustify/builds/plain/build.ninja): the libgit2.so library, and the git2 CLI executable, whose link line names the same libgit2, util and deps objects and src/cli's 17 TUs, so that its link unit holds src/cli's modules and depends on libgit2. One module per translation unit a link line names, with the headers carrying the TU's name and its tests, the shared headers (include/git2/types.h, common.h, cert.h, odb_backend.h, sys/odb_backend.h, sys/refdb_backend.h, sys/stream.h, deps/xdiff/xdiff.h, xtypes.h, ...) split item by item with the file entries' items lists, and a header module for each header implementing what no TU does (src/util/integer.h, array.h, bitvec.h, hashmap.h, hashmap_str.h, staticstr.h, cc-compat.h, ctype_compat.h, strnlen.h, src/libgit2/stream.h, src/libgit2/common.h, deps/ntlmclient/utf8.h, compat.h, deps/xdiff/xmacros.h, src/cli/error.h). Every entity is placed under its C kind, as wavefront 88793d7 schedules it: a shared header's API macro goes to the module whose logic it implements, as the functions it calls and the types it accesses show, a constant or a family of flags to the module owning the type that holds its values or, holding none, whose functions consume it; a function pointer written inline, named by its signature, goes with the struct or function whose declaration holds it; a typedef of its own to the module whose functions use it most; a header holding only macros and typedefs is bundled with the TU it is named for or implements (assert_safe.h and the error-checking macros of git2_util.h with src/util/errors.c, version.h with src/libgit2/libgit2.c, reftable-system.h with deps/reftable/system.c, auth_ntlm.h with auth_ntlmclient.c, src/util/hash/sha.h with src/util/hash.c, unix/pthread.h with src/util/thread.c). Attribute, linkage and configuration macros are not API, and no module owns them (crustify/artifacts/planner/run-8/compose/not_api.json). The TUs the configured build compiles empty are configured out: src/libgit2/streams/openssl_dynamic.c, openssl_legacy.c, schannel.c, stransport.c, src/libgit2/transports/auth_gssapi.c, auth_sspi.c, ssh_exec.c and winhttp.c, and src/cli/win32/. The test executables' sources (tests/libgit2, tests/util) are tests, each listed by the modules whose subject it is, as specs/planning/decomposition.md's Bundling describes: those whose internals it uses (the fields or layout of the types they own, macro expansions included, and their static functions and static globals) and those whose own results or effects its assertions check, the subject area its suite is named for (crustify/artifacts/planner/run-8/compose/areas.py) that its code reaches, the macros it expands included. A test file is split by test function where its tests divide between modules; a clar test case's code includes the static helpers of its file it calls and its suite's __initialize and __cleanup. A test case whose body the configured build compiles empty (a GIT_WIN32-only body, a deprecated API's under GIT_DEPRECATE_HARD, an #if the configuration drops, or a comment alone; 95 of them, crustify/artifacts/planner/run-11/compose/empty11.py) is out of scope, as a configured-out translation unit is: it is tied to no module, a file whose every test case is empty is listed by none, and an entry that ties a file whole names its out-of-scope cases as excluded (planner run 11). deps/clar is the harness every test links, a fixture rather than a test, and is tied to no module. Out of scope, and so owned by no module: the deprecated items (deprecated.h, cred_helpers.h, sys/cred.h and the GIT_DEPRECATE_HARD blocks of the other public headers, such as git_oid_fromstr and git_blame_get_hunk_count) and the declarations the configured build never defines (git_transport_dummy, git_blame_file_from_buffer, git_tree_cache_free, ...): no module's file entries select them, and the schedule seeds of crustify/wavefront/configs/wavefront-config.json leave them out. Each module's objective is the campaign's, port, but for the seven foundational modules, which are wrap in every campaign; a module the standard library or a crate replaces with full parity is ported onto it, as its rust_equivalent records. Each link unit's rust_equivalent records the closest the standard library comes to it as a whole and the crates that could replace it outright: none, since gix and its gix-* components reimplement the target and git2 and libgit2-sys bind it. The seven foundational modules hold the allocators, releasers and cloners of type-erased memory and of strings (src/util/alloc.c, the four src/util/allocators/, deps/reftable/basics.c and src/util/strlist.c), each foundational whole. depends_on holds one record per in-tree module and per out-of-tree library a module depends on, counted from a wavefront 88793d7 schedule of the whole closure (crustify/wavefront/configs/wavefront-config.json without its schedule_seeds, the body-deep graph) over the kinds the modules schema counts, structs, unions, functions, globals and function pointers, at both ends of an edge: an in-tree record's outgoing_edges are the unit edges from this module to the other, its incoming_edges those back, non-zero on either side of a cycle, and its counters the distinct entities it consumes there, by kind; an out-of-tree record counts the distinct entities its units reference from the library whose installed headers define them, as dependencies.json names it, macros and compiler builtins left out. Enums, macros and typedefs of their own are counted nowhere yet, so a module that uses only another's enums, macros or typedefs has no record of it. counters.*.function_pointers counts the function pointers a module owns, declared by a typedef or written inline. Which dependencies the order keeps and which it cuts is schedule.json's. counters.loc counts nonblank, noncomment lines of each owned entity's span: its definition in the TU or an internal header, its declaration or definition in an API header. Every path is below the C root, c/.

std.notes: the operating-system and data-structure layer only: files, paths, processes, TCP sockets, maps, locks and strings. Nothing of git itself: no object database, loose or packed objects, delta compression, index, references or reflogs, configuration files, diff, blame, merge, checkout, rebase or the smart and local transports, and no SHA-1, SHA-256, zlib or TLS, which the target takes from its out-of-tree libraries

no replaceable allocator hooks (reftable_set_alloc) for the C that keeps allocating through them; reftable_buf maps to Vec<u8>, binsearch to binary_search_by, the big-endian helpers to from_be_bytes/to_be_bytes

allocates by Layout rather than by size and aborts on allocation failure through handle_alloc_error, where git__malloc returns NULL and records an out-of-memory error; the replaceable git_allocator vtable installed through GIT_OPT_SET_ALLOCATOR, which C keeps calling, has a counterpart only in #[global_allocator], fixed at link time
no size-prefixed blocks, no poisoning of freed memory and no failure on zero-length allocations
GlobalAlloc takes a Layout and has no file/line arguments; the vtable shape git_allocator expects is not provided

crates.notes: parses request and response heads only, without the callback-driven body, chunked transfer-encoding and keep-alive state machine llhttp generates; no lenient-parsing flags
no settings/callback API (llhttp_settings_t), pause/resume or error-reason reporting
no keep-alive or message-needs-EOF decisions after the head

std.notes: case-insensitive comparisons and searches (utf8casecmp, utf8casestr) and utf8makevalid have no direct counterparts; ASCII-only case mapping differs from str::to_lowercase

crates.notes: an SSPI-shaped NTLM implementation: no ntlm_client_* message API, and its own credential and target-name handling
NTLMv2 message construction only; small, single-maintainer crate without the LM/NTLMv1 paths or the client state machine
MD4 only
HMAC only, with md-5 for HMAC-MD5
DES only; random bytes need a separate RNG

std.notes: String::from_utf16 rejects unpaired surrogates rather than reporting the position; no ntlm_unicode_ctx
no fixed error-code-to-string table
BinaryHeap is a max-heap over Ord; the merged-iterator ordering by record key and table index needs a custom Ord, and removal of arbitrary entries is not supported
an unbalanced binary search tree keyed by a comparison callback; BTreeMap needs Ord keys

crates.notes: tokenization and line hashing are internal to the crate; no mmfile, chastore or emit-record helpers
its interner replaces record classification, without xdiff's whitespace-ignoring hash variants

std.notes: no version-checked option structures

crates.notes: no callback-driven execution over a partial buffer
the unavoidable-bit-condition check is internal to the crate
collision detection and the safe-hash mode match; no collision callback (SHA1DCSetCallback) and no switch to disable UBC checks

std.notes: thread_local! keys are static; git_tlsdata keys are created at runtime with a destructor

crates.notes: per-object thread-local values only, as git_tlsdata_* provide; no threads, mutexes, read-write locks, condition variables or atomics, which only the standard library provides

std.notes: no thread-local last-error record with class codes, no saved and restored error state

crates.notes: pure Rust, with the same SHA-256 output; no OpenSSL engine selection
a common Digest trait, with sha1-checked and sha2 as its SHA-1 and SHA-256; no algorithm-tagged context or hex formatting
the same engine and semantics, but patterns are &str, so the non-UTF-8 patterns git_regexp_compile accepts cannot be compiled
a different engine: no backreferences or lookaround that PCRE2 patterns may use
Myers and histogram only, no patience, no whitespace-ignoring flags, no indent heuristic or hunk compaction; output differs in hunk placement
Myers, patience and LCS without histogram or xdiff's heuristics

included: int (*)(void *, long, long, long, long, const char *, long)

crates.notes: unified-diff formatting without function-name context lines (find_func) or xdiff's hunk callbacks
its histogram algorithm differs in fallback and tie-breaking, so hunks can differ
three-way merge without xdiff's merge levels, favor modes, zealous conflict reduction or diff3 marker styles
patience diff without xdiff's fallback to Myers on unique-line failure

std.notes: no reference-counted init/shutdown with registered shutdown callbacks
no out-of-memory sentinel state, no base85/base64/hex/quoting helpers, no git_str_rtrim/unquote etc.

crates.notes: covers git_str_encode_base64/decode_base64 only

std.notes: git_buf is C-owned storage handed across the API; no NUL-terminated ptr/size/reserved layout

crates.notes: a global logger with levels; git_trace_set installs one callback with libgit2's own levels (fatal..trace) and a minimum level, which map onto log::Level only approximately
parses RFC 2822/3339 and strict formats; no git approxidate (relative dates, "yesterday", "noon") or git's offset formats
RFC 2822 parsing and offset arithmetic only; no approxidate

maps files shared, private or read-only at any offset (p_mmap, p_munmap); no page-size or mapping-alignment query (git__page_size, git__mmap_alignment), which mwindow sizes its windows by: its page_size() is private
a bump arena without git_pool's fixed item size, string helpers (git_pool_strdup/strcat) or pointer-in-pool test

std.notes: git_utf8_iterate decodes one code point and reports invalid sequences as -1; str::from_utf8 validates whole buffers
strtol variants with git's overflow handling, git__strntolower, git__prefixcmp and the other string helpers map onto str methods individually

crates.notes: hex encoding and decoding only; no object-id type, shortening (git_oid_shorten) or SHA-1/SHA-256 tagging
WHATWG URLs: no scp-like git URLs (git_net_url_parse_scp), no redirect application or git's default ports and validity rules
covers the Basic credential encoding only, not the auth-context scheme
xoshiro256** itself; libgit2 seeds it from time, pid and getentropy

std.notes: no git path normalization (git_fs_path_squash_slashes, prettify), .git ownership checks or case-folding comparisons

crates.notes: home and XDG config directories; no git search-path lists (global, xdg, system, programdata, template) set through GIT_OPT_SET_SEARCH_PATH

std.notes: covers the file operations; p_* wrappers retry on EINTR and set libgit2 errors

crates.license: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT
crates.notes: safe syscalls without libgit2's error reporting

std.notes: no block-source vtable or mmap-backed reads
no recursive mkdir with base-path and permission policy, rmdir_r flags, fake-mtime handling or file-stamp tracking

crates.notes: temporary files only
atomic replace on commit; no git .lock-file protocol, streamed zlib deflate or SHA-1 hashing of the written content

included: int (*)(git_odb_backend *, const git_oid *, const void *, size_t, git_object_t)
int (*)(git_odb_stream **, size_t *, git_object_t *, git_odb_backend *, const git_oid *)
int (*)(git_oid *, void **, size_t *, git_object_t *, git_odb_backend *, const git_oid *, size_t)
int (*)(void **, size_t *, git_object_t *, git_odb_backend *, const git_oid *)

std.notes: case-insensitive keying of index entries needs a custom Hash/Eq

crates.notes: parses plain unified diffs; no git extended headers (renames, modes, index lines) or binary patches

included: int (*)(git_refdb_backend *, const char *, const git_oid *, const char *)
int (*)(git_refdb_backend *, const git_reference *, int, const git_signature *, const char *, const git_oid *, const char *)
int (*)(git_refdb_backend *, void *, int, int, const git_reference *, const git_signature *, const char *)
int (*)(git_reference **, git_refdb_backend *, const char *, const char *, int, const git_signature *, const char *)

std.notes: git_pqueue optionally caps its size and keeps the smallest items, sorting with a comparison callback
covers spawn, pipes, environment and wait; no git_process_result_msg formatting

crates.notes: glob syntax close to wildmatch but not identical in "**" and bracket handling; no WM_PATHNAME/WM_CASEFOLD flags as such
only "*" and "?"; no brackets, "**" or path semantics
gitignore-style pattern matching only; no attribute assignments or macros
gitignore matching (gitignore::Gitignore) without libgit2's repository-scoped rule stack, git_ignore_add_rule or core.excludesfile lookup
glob matching without git pathspec magic or git_pathspec_match_list results
three-way text merge without xdiff's favor modes, marker sizes or diff3 style
Compress/Decompress cover deflate and inflate streams; no deflateBound for sizing output, and git_zstream_get_output's chunked loop is the caller's
applies a unified patch to text; no index/workdir targets, binary patches or git_apply_options callbacks
memory maps only; no window cache with global mapped-memory and open-file limits

std.notes: no git_stream vtable and no connect timeout policy from GIT_OPT_SET_SERVER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT applied through poll

crates.notes: SslStream over any Read + Write covers the TLS session and verification; no git_stream vtable, no git certificate-check callback contract or cipher defaults
platform TLS without custom CA-file locations per call or access to the peer X509 for git_cert_x509
an HTTP/1.1 client without git's proxy and credential-retry loop, certificate callbacks or streaming over a git_stream
HTTP machinery without a client policy for git's auth negotiation and redirects

std.notes: the generic open-addressing map and set the macros mint per key and value type (khash's), with the hash and equality functions each instance names: HashMap<K, V, S> and HashSet<K, S> with a BuildHasher cover them, but not the C instances' layout, their iterator as a bare bucket index (git_hashmap_iter_t) that survives insertions, or a per-instance equality function other than Eq

crates.notes: the SwissTable map the standard library's HashMap is built on; its raw table API gives bucket indices and custom hash and equality closures (HashTable), closer to the instances' find, put and remove by key, but its buckets move on growth as khash's do and it has no khash layout either

std.notes: the size_t printf formats (PRIuZ, PRIxZ, PRIXZ, PRIdZ) are core::fmt's {} and {:x}; GIT_UNUSED is `let _ = x;`; va_copy is VaList::clone, which is unstable (c_variadic)

the u8 ASCII predicates and case maps are the C locale's; the macros call <ctype.h>, which follows the process locale (libgit2 runs in the C locale unless its caller sets another), and isspace counts the vertical tab, which is_ascii_whitespace does not; isprint is is_ascii_graphic or b' '

crates.notes: memchr(0, &buf[..n]) is p_strnlen's bounded scan for the terminating NUL, vectorized

std.notes: argument access, exit codes and standard streams only: no option parsing or usage output (src/cli/opt.c, opt_usage.c), no progress reporting, no signal handling, and none of the commands, which call libgit2

crates.notes: subcommand dispatch by name through its own Command builder, not the cli_cmd_spec table of entry points, briefs and help flags
parses the common options and dispatches subcommands, but with its own usage and error text, not the cli_opt specs' GNU-style reordering, --help/--version handling or pager option

argument parsing from a declared spec, but not cli_opt_spec's model (switch, value, literal, arg and args kinds, choice groups, required and optional-value flags) or its status codes and GNU-style reordering
a low-level short/long option tokenizer with no spec table, choices, required checks or status reporting
generates usage and help text, in its own layout rather than cli_opt_usage_fprint's and cli_opt_help_fprint's, without the hidden and choice-group rendering they apply
progress bars with throttled redraws, but not the git-style fetch, indexer and checkout lines, sideband passthrough or the deferred-line buffering cli_progress keeps
runs the interrupt handler on its own thread rather than from the SIGINT handler, and cannot be reset to the default disposition (cli_sighandler_set_interrupt(NULL))

std.notes: formats to standard error, but has no cli_error_git reporting of git_error_last() or the CLI_EXIT_ERROR/CLI_EXIT_USAGE codes these return
